$comment: The Appearance section's Sidebar rows and the workspace row rows (sidebar.workspaceRow.*; the per-kind lists stay off the page). The hover cards and Now Playing rows (their own sources) follow the sidebar list in SettingsSchema.all.

help.text: Separate shades the sidebar darker than the main pane.
A line on the sidebar's edge. Off, the edge shows a line only while you hover or drag it.
How the sections above and below the workspace list draw.
The share of the sidebar the top sections fill before they scroll.
The share of the sidebar the bottom sections fill before they scroll.
Off: the top and bottom sections never scroll and the workspace list gets smaller.

title.text: Show All Chats on New Tab

help.text: New Tab lists every agent chat on this computer, not only recent ones.
Lists workspaces an agent started under the workspace that started them.

The id of an installed extension that draws the whole workspace list (cmux.sidebar/1), such as local/workspace-list. Empty draws the built-in list, which also shows while the extension loads, fails or is removed.

rows.note: Group by Folder's rows with no folder sit at the end of the list with no No Folder header (SidebarLayout's folder loop; customize-app-profiles, the Claude Code app's look). Off by default: the No Folder header shows as before.

help.text: Under Group by Folder, rows with no folder sit at the end of the list with no No Folder header.

rows.note: The nav block a look puts at the top of the sidebar: plain icon and label rows that run cmux actions. Rust validates it (cmux-layout-reducer sidebar_nav.rs); empty draws no block.

help.text: Rows at the top of the sidebar that run cmux actions, by action id, optionally "id | Title | symbol". Empty shows none.

rows.page_hidden: action ids; cmux.json, setups and theme files only

help.text: Spaces show once you have more than one. New Space is in the command palette.
A search button after the profile button. Off: search from the palette.

rows.note: Off by default (Lawrence 2026-11-25: "get rid of it by default... keep things as minimal as possible"; Leo 2026-11-25 didn't want it on by default either; Leo 2026-11-24 first asked for an icon "somewhere omnipresent"). Off hides the footer's Live button only; presence.live and the Live palette action stay.

help.text: A Live button after the profile button turns presence on or off. Off: use the palette.

rows.name: presenceLive
rows.note: Off by default (RFD 0141: Live is opt-in, nothing about a person leaves their machine until they turn it on). On: this Mac publishes its presence and the footer's Live button is accent-filled; off it is dimmed. The daemon reads the same key from cmux.json.

help.text: Show teammates and agents who are live, and let them see you. Off: you appear offline.
A chevron beside the + opens the New Workspace menu. Off: right-click the +.
Each workspace is one line in the sidebar, which stays a list (not a tab strip), and Cmd-Shift-[ and ] switch workspaces as they switch tabs.
Groups get a colored rail with a rounded end, like Chrome's tab groups.
Drag a workspace row onto a pane's edge to show it beside the current one.
Stops the sidebar's edges fading and hides the bottom profile and search bar.

title.text: Show Sidebar Controls Only on Hover

help.text: The sidebar's buttons show only while the pointer is over it.
With the sidebar hidden, point at the window's edge to show it over your work.
Sidebar and tab bar buttons show only while the pointer is over them.
Rows, headers and status marks like another app's sidebar. Your own sidebar settings still win.
Rail shrinks the sidebar to a strip; point at it to open the full sidebar.

rows.note: On: the sidebar's right-click and more-button menus open as cmux-drawn menus (GlassMenu) with the same rows, shortcuts, submenus and keys, so the menu look (appearance.menu.*) styles them; off (the default) keeps the system menu, which cannot be restyled. A look pack or a theme file turns it on; it applies to the next menu opened.

help.text: Right-click and more-button menus in the sidebar follow the menu look instead of the system menu.
Expanded shows status, age, pull request and computer under each name.
Makes the sidebar's names, icons and rows larger together.
What the profile button at the sidebar's foot opens: the app menu, or an account menu with your accounts and teams to switch between, then Settings, Usage, Help and Sign Out.
Icons for working, waiting, error and done. Off: a spinner and a dot.
Rows show when they last changed, such as 3d.

rows.note: Seen, finished agent chats fold behind a Settled (N) row at the end of their list (SidebarLayout+DoneFold); the rule is Rust's (cmux-layout-reducer settle). Off by default; the Studio look turns it on.

help.text: A chat whose answer you have read folds into Settled at the end of its list until its next turn.

rows.note: Leo 2026-11-25 about the nested helper sessions: "idk who asked for those in teh sidebar. it's weird". Off by default: a workspace whose session another session's agent started (acpmux spawnedBy, a peer daemon's parents, AgentSessionParents) draws no row, except one waiting on the person (a permission or a question) and the selected one, which draw under their parents (SidebarSessionTreeState.hidesStarted). On nests them under their parents (the lineage nesting that was Debug's sidebar.lineageNesting).

help.text: Sessions an agent starts list under the session that started them. Off, they stay in the parent chat's list; one that needs you still shows.
How a workspace's color shows in the sidebar.
With more than one computer, this Mac's workspaces show its icon too.
A collapsed group shows how many workspaces it holds.
A collapsed group shows its unread notification count.
How a group draws. Folders shows plain folders; Sections shows plain headings.
Where group colors come from. A color you pick for a group stays.
The gradient Group Colors uses when set to Gradient.
Hides the chosen sections until the pointer is over the sidebar.
A daily card shows one cmux feature you have not used yet.

summary.text: A daily tip about a feature you haven't used

help.text: A bell listing every agent chat, the ones waiting on you first.

summary.text: Agent chats that need you, at the top of the sidebar

help.text: The sidebar bell's state while the Priority view is on. Off, the sidebar is unchanged.
All, Waiting, Unread and Running chips with counts, and Mark All as Read.
Off, Priority lists only chats that need you or are running.
Each Priority row says its state, such as Needs you or Done.
On the right, the window buttons sit over the tab bar.
Distance between the centers of neighboring Space buttons. The density default fits them to the sidebar.
Under the window buttons or above the Settings row.
On Hover hides the spaces with the other sidebar controls.
Control-1 to 9 selects the other one.

summary.text: Workspaces or tabs on Command-1 to 9

help.text: Every Item: Home is Command-1. Workspaces Only: the first workspace is Command-1.

summary.text: What Command-1 to Command-9 go to

help.text: Goes to the last item, as in browsers, or to the ninth.
What Command-Control-] and Command-Control-[ step through.
Past the last item, the next item is the first again.

rows.name: sectionsHidden
rows.note: Sidebar sections to leave out, by section id or stable key (cmux-layout-reducer sidebar_section_customization.rs plans the projection; SidebarProjectionCustomizationResolver reads it; docs/cmux-next/sidebar-customization.md).

help.text: Sidebar sections to hide, by id. The section of the selected workspace always shows.

rows.name: sectionsOrder
rows.note: Sidebar sections first in their region (top, middle, bottom), by section id or stable key; never across regions (sidebar_section_customization.rs).

help.text: Sidebar sections to show first in their part of the sidebar, in this order, by id.
The icon or emoji you chose for a workspace.
The terminal's title, which the shell or program sets.
The status agents and hooks report, one line each.
Set by a hook: cmux workspace status set ports <text>.
Set by a hook: cmux workspace status set pr <text>.
A progress bar under the row and the busy mark of running work.
A mark while an agent works in the workspace.
The newest line agents and scripts log: cmux workspace log append <text>.

summary.text: Newest line agents and scripts log

help.text: The text of the workspace's newest unread notification.
The order of the shown items under the workspace name.
Where the row's status mark draws: at the row's end, or before the name in the icon's place.
The lines each workspace row shows, as lists of items, such as [["icon", "name", "branch"], ["agentStatus"]]. Up to 3 lines of 6 items; the name always leads the first line.

rows.palette_hidden: the Sidebar page's row layout editor edits it (CMUX-383): the palette has no nested-JSON value page

help.text: A row layout for each kind of workspace: terminal, agent, browser or mixed. It wins over Row Layout.

rows.palette_hidden: the Sidebar page's row layout editor edits it (CMUX-383): the palette has no nested-JSON value page

help.text: A row layout for each agent, by agent id such as claude or codex. It wins over the other row layouts.

rows.palette_hidden: the Sidebar page's row layout editor edits it (CMUX-383): the palette has no nested-JSON value page
